answer: Identity bonds that decay. Each agent locks a 60-credit bond to join; it sheds 5 credits per epoch, like a plume of smoke thinning, and vanishes after 12 epochs unless renewed by verified work. A renewal must echo its earlier record, so a copied identity cannot pass. Forging 100 identities costs 6,000 credits, and the bonds keep bleeding, so fakes starve before they earn. An honest agent pays once and holds its ledge while fakes slip off.
